title: Vitalé Labs 'Balance Brief' 3-episode drop: quick-cut a landscape highlight and reframe a vertical Reel from each 4K take, grade three cover stills to one channel look, then data-merge a 3-card episode carousel

source.reference: Engaging Video Editor for GEN Checkup

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com short-form-video brief for a health/wellness/genetics channel wanting 'educational, engaging, social-media driven' Reels/Shorts and someone comfortable with 'pacing, and social-media style'. The real company/person are laundered to the fictional IP-clean brand 'Vitalé Labs', its mini-series 'The Balance Brief', and presenter persona 'Dr. Nadia Reuter'; no real brand, product, person, or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the literal brief implies open-timeline Premiere/After Effects work (multi-track compositing, motion graphics, burned-in animated subtitles, word-level semantic trimming) which is NOT in connector scope, so the job is re-cast to the genuinely-doable slice the brief rewards AND scaled up from a single clip to a real three-episode content drop. The client shot SIX raw takes across THREE episode topics (two takes per episode — one presenter-to-camera A-take, one silent coverage B-take), filmed on three different days under three different lighting setups, at 3840x2160 (4K) on a mirrorless camera — each PRESENTER take a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE real camera recording full of restarts, lost threads, note-checking pauses and dead air (NOT a short AI-generated clip), so a highlight cut has far more than 15 seconds of raw material to SHORTEN down from — with an 18% grey reference card clipped to the desk edge for the whole of every take. The Adobe chain does the real, in-scope work: for each episode, auto-cut its PRESENTER take into a punchy LANDSCAPE highlight (video_create_quick_cut, which shortens a SINGLE supplied clip by visual engagement — NOT a semantic/script-driven cut and NOT an assembly of multiple clips), and reframe that episode's 4K presenter take to a 1080x1920 vertical Reel (video_resize on the 4K TAKE — a same-length, no-stretch 9:16 crop that DOWNSCALES from the 4K frame, never upscaled and never sourced from the 1080p highlight); then pull a hero cover still from each episode's presenter take, grade the three covers to ONE cohesive channel look against each frame's grey card (a different correction per day), prep-and-vectorize the channel wordmark, and data-merge the three episodes into a three-card social carousel deck. No timeline trims-to-timecode, no motion graphics, no burned-in captions, no compositing, and no upscaling are claimed.
one_line_ask: For each of Vitalé Labs' three episodes, cut a punchy landscape highlight from its presenter take and reframe a 1080x1920 vertical Reel from the 4K take (never upscaled), pull and grade a hero cover still so all three read as one channel look at a common white point, vectorize the channel wordmark, and data-merge a three-card episode carousel deck — one card per episode.
full_brief: Vitalé Labs runs an educational wellness channel and we are dropping a three-episode mini-series, 'The Balance Brief', about how personalized nutrition works. We filmed it over three days and it shows: each episode was shot in a different room under different light, and every take has our scientist Dr. Nadia Reuter rambling, restarting sentences, and pausing to check her notes. For each of the three episodes you have two raw takes — a presenter-to-camera A-take and a silent coverage B-take — six 3840x2160 (4K) files in total, shot on a mirrorless camera, the presenter takes each running a couple of minutes of raw, unedited talking with the fluffs and pauses left in. On the desk edge of every take we left an 18% grey reference card and a small white chip so white balance can be reconciled after the fact. What we need back is a clean, premium, trustworthy set — educational, NOT flashy or meme-style. Deliverables and the bar: (1) Per episode, TWO short-form edits — a punchy LANDSCAPE highlight cut down from that episode's presenter take to the strongest, most watchable ~15 seconds with the dead air and restarts dropped (16:9), AND a VERTICAL 9:16 version of that episode for Reels and Shorts, delivered at exactly 1080x1920 with no stretching and no upscaling; you have the full-resolution 4K takes, so the vertical must be reframed from source that genuinely holds that many vertical pixels — a Reel that has been blown up looks soft and we will reject it; (2) THREE episode COVER stills — one strong hero cover frame per episode, each showing the presenter, graded so all three read as ONE consistent channel look: every frame's grey reference card must read truly neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at one common white point, all three sharing a single deep black point, with skin kept natural and the window highlight not blown. The three episodes were shot on different days under different light, so getting all three to match at the grey card is the whole job — a carousel whose covers don't sit at one white point looks cheap and we will reject it. Hand back, per cover, a retained card-bearing neutralized master with the grey reference card still in frame as your neutrality proof; then crop the grey card out for the finished cover, each a 4:5 portrait card image. (3) Our channel WORDMARK only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — clean it up and turn it into crisp vector art for the card header and our channel avatar. (4) Finally, build the CAROUSEL: we hand you our authored InDesign episode-card template and an episode sheet; merge them so each episode gets its own card with its graded cover placed, the wordmark in the header, and the episode number, title, hook line and runtime set in type — one card per episode, exported as a carousel deck. Along with the files, hand back a short sheet listing, per cover, the white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure and black-point you dialed, so we can confirm the covers were matched to one target and not eyeballed. Bind the card copy verbatim from our episode sheet — do not rewrite our titles or hooks.

inputs.name: ep01_hydration_take_A_presenter.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CLIENT-SUPPLIED REAL CAMERA FOOTAGE (a full-length raw take — cannot be model-generated, and deliberately NOT an ~8s AI-gen clip): a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE single-take static-tripod talking-head recording, 3840x2160 (4K) landscape, shot on a mirrorless camera, of a calm professional woman in her early 40s (fictional nutrition scientist 'Dr. Nadia Reuter') in a lab coat over a knit top, seated at a light-wood desk in a modern office, talking through hydration and genetics conversationally to camera for the full two-to-three minutes. Across the long take she restarts several sentences, loses her thread once or twice, and pauses to glance down at her notes — leaving stretches of dead air and fluffed lines around a handful of strong, clean, watchable moments, so a highlight has far more than 15 seconds of raw material to be cut DOWN from. Shot in the EVENING under WARM tungsten work-light with a distinct orange cast and slightly bright exposure. An 18% neutral grey reference card and a small white chip rest flat on the desk at the lower-left edge of frame for the WHOLE take. Realistic imperfect handheld-YouTube feel, decent-not-studio lighting, natural skin, no captions, no lower-thirds, no on-screen graphics. This is REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI and NOT an AI-generated clip. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks on any object, screen, device, product, bottle label or clothing — all labels plain blank/fictional.
inputs.realism_notes: Episode 1 (Hydration), Session A — WARM/orange, bright. A REAL ~2-3 minute client camera take (restarts, note-checking pauses, dead air), FAR longer than the ~15s highlight — this is why it is declared as genuine multi-minute camera footage and not an ~8s veo-3/AI-gen clip: video_create_quick_cut can only SHORTEN a single supplied clip (output duration < source), so the source must genuinely run minutes. This presenter A-take is the SINGLE source for episode 1's three video products: its landscape highlight (video_create_quick_cut shortens this ONE long clip to ~15s), its 1080x1920 vertical Reel (video_resize reframes THIS 4K take same-length — a downscale, never the 1080p highlight), and its hero cover still (it carries the face and the in-frame grey card). Its warm cast means the cover grade must correct the opposite direction to episode 2. Grey card at the desk edge for the whole take so any pulled frame contains the neutralisation target; the card is cropped out of the finished 4:5 cover. 4K so the vertical reframe and the 4:5 card-crop are both honest downscales.

inputs.name: vitale_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the fictional channel wordmark 'VITALÉ LABS' inked on off-white textured paper: a clean humanist sans wordmark with a small three-leaf sprig glyph, deep teal-ink letters. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. No real trademarks.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 deg skew, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/separate from the ground, crop to the mark, knock the off-white to transparency, THEN vectorize. Feeds the card masthead (via the merge) and doubles as the channel-avatar vector master.

inputs.name: balance_brief_episode_cards.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built single-record InDesign episode-card template (.indd/.idml), one card per page at 1080x1350 px (4:5 portrait, social-carousel card, RGB). It contains live data-merge placeholder fields <<episode_no>>, <<title>>, <<hook>>, <<runtime>>, a masthead image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path column (@logo) for the vector wordmark, and a large cover image frame wired to a second @-prefixed image-path column (@cover) so the merge drops each episode's graded cover into its card. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid — document_merge_data_layout emits one page per row, so the template holds exactly one card's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it produces ONE PAGE PER ROW — so a single-card template merged against a 3-row sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape for a 3-card carousel. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced. The template layout is the client's; the distinctive quality of each card — the cohesive matched cover grade — is the agent's work.

inputs.name: balance_brief_episode_sheet.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a 3-row data-merge CSV, one row per episode, with columns episode_no,title,hook,runtime,@cover,@logo. Row 1: episode_no 'EP 01', title 'Hydration & Your Genes', hook 'Your water needs are written in your DNA — here's how to read them.', runtime '0:15'. Row 2: episode_no 'EP 02', title 'Sleep, Cortisol & Recovery', hook 'Why your recovery stalls at 2am — and the nutrient timing that helps.', runtime '0:15'. Row 3: episode_no 'EP 03', title 'Vitamin D & Absorption', hook 'You take it daily. Your genes decide if it lands.', runtime '0:15'. The @cover cell of each row names that episode's graded cover file (e.g. @ep01_cover_graded.jpg); the @logo cell holds the SAME vector wordmark file in all three rows. Column names must exactly match the template fields <<episode_no>>,<<title>>,<<hook>>,<<runtime>> and the @cover / @logo image columns. Restrained, professional wellness tone, no medical cure claims.
inputs.realism_notes: The @cover column is the binding contract — the agent must point each row at its own produced graded cover so document_merge_data_layout places the right cover on the right card; the @logo column (constant) places the vectorized wordmark in every masthead. Row count = 3 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the WRONG tool here because it cannot bind the @cover / @logo image columns.

inputs.name: vitale_brand_kit.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a compact one-page brand-kit PDF for a fictional wellness channel 'Vitalé Labs': primary colours (deep teal #0F5C5B, warm sand #E9DCC7, ink #1B1B1B), a clean humanist sans wordmark, tone words 'clean, modern, educational, trustworthy, not flashy', social handle @vitalelabs, and the delivery specs — Reels 1080x1920 (9:16), carousel cards 1080x1350 (4:5). No stock logos or real trademarks.
inputs.realism_notes: Provides the brand constraints, the channel look words the cover grade must serve, and the exact export dimensions referenced in the brief, IP-clean and fictional.

outputs.name: ep01_hydration_highlight_1080p.mp4

The 9:16 crop of a 2160-tall frame is ~1215 px wide (>=1080), so resizing it to 1080x1920 is an honest DOWNSCALE. outputs.name: ep02_sleep_reel_1080x1920.mp4

outputs.name: episode_cover_masters_x3
outputs.spec: Three RETAINED card-bearing neutralized cover MASTERS (EP01/EP02/EP03), one hero frame pulled from each episode's presenter A-take and graded to ONE channel look with the in-frame 18% grey card STILL PRESENT: the grey card neutralised (R≈G≈B) at one common white point across all three, a shared black-point (deep, not clipped to 0), skin natural, window highlight not blown. These masters (card in frame) are the artifacts on which grey-card neutrality is graded — the grader measures channel spread on the card here, never on the cropped crop. Full-res sRGB, retained as a delivered QC artifact. Accompanied by a per-cover parameter sheet (temperature/tint, exposure, black-point the agent dialed by eye) proving the three were matched to one target, non-identical across the three lighting days. These delivered crops are checked ONLY for card-EXCLUSION (the reference card must not appear) and correct 4:5 1080x1350 dimensions — neutrality is graded on the retained card-bearing masters above, never on these card-cropped files. Each feeds its episode's @cover cell in the carousel merge.

outputs.name: vitale_wordmark.svg

connector_workflow.inputs_from: ep01_hydration_take_A_presenter.mp4, ep01_hydration_take_B_coverage.mp4, ep02_sleep_take_A_presenter.mp4, ep02_sleep_take_B_coverage.mp4, ep03_vitamind_take_A_presenter.mp4, ep03_vitamind_take_B_coverage.mp4, vitale_wordmark_scan.png, balance_brief_episode_cards.indd, balance_brief_episode_sheet.csv, vitale_brand_kit.pdf
connector_workflow.note: Load the six raw 4K takes, the wordmark scan, the authored .indd card template, the episode CSV and the brand kit into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not the difficulty.

TRIAGE + one-clip rule: cut ONLY from episode 1's PRESENTER A-take — a single supplied clip. video_create_quick_cut shortens ONE video to a ~15s landscape highlight by visual-engagement selection (the tool makes the cut, NOT a semantic/script trim); it cannot assemble the A-take and the silent B coverage into one master, so exactly one clip goes in and the source take is far longer than the ~15s target. Cutting from the silent B coverage insert (no face, no watchable presenter moment) would be a visibly wrong highlight. user_prompt = premium educational wellness sizzle, restrained/not-flashy. Produces episode 1's LANDSCAPE highlight (async). DELIVERABLE.

Cut ONLY from episode 2's presenter A-take — one clip, shortened to a ~15s landscape highlight, same restrained brief, visual-engagement selection only. Never assembled with the B coverage. Episode 2 landscape highlight (async). DELIVERABLE.

Cut ONLY from episode 3's presenter A-take — one clip, shortened to a ~15s landscape highlight, visual-engagement selection only. Never assembled with the B coverage. Episode 3 landscape highlight (async). DELIVERABLE.

Reframe episode 1's 4K (3840x2160) PRESENTER take to a 9:16 vertical 1080x1920 Reel — subject-aware, same length, no stretch. Source the vertical from the 4K TAKE, NOT from the 1080p landscape highlight: a 9:16 crop of the 4K frame is ~1215x2160, so downscaling it to 1080x1920 is an honest DOWNSCALE, whereas a 9:16 strip of the 1080p highlight is only ~607x1080 and delivering 1080x1920 from it would be an UPSCALE. Downscale-only, never canvas-extend. DELIVERABLE.

Reframe episode 2's 4K presenter take to 1080x1920 vertical, same length, no stretch. From the 4K TAKE (~1215x2160 9:16 crop -> 1080x1920 downscale), never from the 1080p highlight, never upscaled. DELIVERABLE.
Reframe episode 3's 4K presenter take to 1080x1920 vertical, same length, no stretch. From the 4K TAKE, never from the 1080p highlight, never upscaled. DELIVERABLE.

Pull a hero cover still from episode 1's PRESENTER A-take (the take that carries the face and the in-frame grey card), choosing a strong, engaged, eyes-open frame. Pull from the full-res 4K take — NOT from the 1080p highlight and NOT from the vertical Reel — so the later 4:5 card crop stays an honest downscale rather than an upscale. Pulling from the silent B coverage insert (no face) would be a visibly wrong cover.
Pull a hero cover still from episode 2's presenter A-take, a strong framed moment. From the full-res 4K take, not the cut and not the reframe, for the same downscale reason.
Pull a hero cover still from episode 3's presenter A-take. From the full-res 4K take, not the cut and not the reframe.

ESTABLISH the channel cover look on episode 1 and record it as the shared target. Episode 1 is WARM/orange and bright, so COOL the temperature and nudge tint until its in-frame grey card reads truly neutral, then pull exposure DOWN to the shared brightness and set blacks at the house near-black floor (deep, not clipped). Keep skin natural, protect the window highlight. Authored from primitives — NOT a preset, NOT auto-tone. Report the temp/tint/exposure/black chosen — these define the common target the other two covers must hit. This card-bearing full-res result is RETAINED as episode 1's neutrality-grading master (grey card still in frame); the later crop removes the card and is not graded for neutrality.

Grade episode 2's cover to the SAME target — the OPPOSITE-direction correction. It is COOL/blue and flat/under, so WARM the temperature to neutralise its grey card to the common white point and LIFT exposure to the shared brightness, then seat the same black floor. Copying episode 1's cooling/pull-down numbers here is exactly the trap that fails the match. Report its distinct values.

Episode 3 was shot under balanced neutral light, so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral and its exposure is right — the correct move is to HOLD white balance (no cast shift) and only seat the shared black floor / match brightness by a hair. A naive agent that batch-applies episode 1's cooling, or 'cools an imagined cast', pushes an already-correct cover off-neutral and breaks the matched set. Decision must be driven by THIS card. Report that WB was held.

Crop episode 1's graded MASTER (ep01_cover_graded_fullres, the retained card-bearing neutrality artifact) to the 4:5 portrait card frame, cropping the lower-left grey/white reference card OUT of the finished cover in the same move, and resize to 1080x1350. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the 4K frame — never canvas-extend, never upscale. This crop is graded for card-EXCLUSION only; neutrality was graded on the retained master. Feeds the @cover cell for EP01. DELIVERABLE (cover crop set).
Crop episode 2's graded cover to 4:5, grey card out, resize to 1080x1350. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @cover cell for EP02.

Crop episode 3's graded cover to 4:5, grey card out, resize to 1080x1350. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the @cover cell for EP03. The three covers now share one white point, each neutralised to its own grey card.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward clean white so the teal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the surrounding paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and sprig glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the card masthead and the channel avatar. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE.
